title: Stop falling for these Ab Training Myths
summary: First in a myth-busting series: NH attacks 'abs are made in the kitchen', the idea that compounds and bracing build abs, the claim that sit-ups hurt the back, the EMG-based dismissal of leg raises, and the fear that ab and oblique training thickens the waist. Abs are a muscle like any other and must be trained directly, with range of motion, every week for years.
claims: 'Abs are made in the kitchen' is wrong: getting lean only reveals abs, and like any muscle they must be trained to grow
Naturals who never train abs must diet extremely lean to see them; that is a muscularity problem, not a leanness problem
Train abs while bulking even if you can't see them, so they show sooner when you cut
Trained abs stay visible year-round because muscularity doesn't vanish the way leanness does
'Diet is 80%' is nonsense; training is 80% or more, and diet shapes the body around the work
Core strength and ab size are different: compounds and bracing give only an isometric contraction without stretch, so they won't build a six-pack
Train abs through a full range with stretch and contraction (sit-ups, windshield wipers), as you would any other muscle
Relying on squats and deadlifts for abs has a terrible stimulus-to-fatigue ratio compared with direct isolation
Like abs, forearms aren't covered by deadlifts and need direct isolation
Sit-ups only hurt the back if you lead with the torso and flex the lumbar spine instead of bending at the hips and using the abs; done properly they are safe
Leg raises do work the abs: the hip flexors initiate, but the abs catch the weight of pelvis and legs and contract on the return
Leg raises made the biggest difference to his lower abs; calisthenics athletes spam them for six-packs regardless of EMG studies
Waist width is mostly genetic and set by bone structure; direct ab and oblique training will not ruin a V-taper
Bodybuilders with thick obliques usually already had big obliques that were fat before turning to muscle; if they thicken, stopping those movements reverses it
Bodybuilder 'pregnant bellies' come from drugs, not ab training; naturals won't have that problem
Isolate your abs every week of every year; patience and consistency are the only way to a six-pack
exercises: bend at the hips, don't lead with the torso or flex the lower back
ab isolation with range of motion
control the legs on the way down, curl back up
lower abs; abs catch the weight of pelvis and legs
